To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the G value (i.e., number of bases released) per 100 eV of absorbed energy from the irradiation of the DNA hydration water is the same for all water molecules of the first hydration layer (gamma less than or equal to 15) and that this G value is 1.5 times greater than the G value for irradiated dry DNA (gamma = 0).

(1) the G value for base release increases linearly with dose up to at least 90 kGY; (2) the G value is not constant as a function of water content but increases with hydration; (3) the G value increases with hydration more rapidly in oxygen than in nitrogen; and (4) the increase in the G value with hydration can be described by a model involving the change in DNA conformation from the A or C conformer to the B conformer and
the release of unalibrated bases from irradiated dry DNA, hydrated between gamma = 2 and 32.8, was linear with dose to 90 kgy, except for the dry DNA, which was linear to only 10 kgy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the role of water in the radiation chemistry of DNA and the elucidation of radiation-induced DNA lesions.
the elucidation of the mechanism of radiation-induced DNA strand breakage.
elucidating the role of water molecules in the radiation chemistry of DNA and the role of DNA in radiation chemistry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the release of free bases is not simply the result of the ionization of the DNA bases or the ionization of water, but rather is the result of a complex interaction between the DNA and the hydration water.

the release of unal altered bases from DNA, hydrated between gamma = 2-32.7 mol H2O/mol nucleotide, is a function of dose (up to approximately 90 kGyr), the extent of hydration, oxygen, and DNA conformation.
, in the absence of oxygen, the release of unal altered bases is the result of a direct ionization of DNA and of hydroxyl radical attack on the DNA and its hydration water.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the yield of unaltered free bases is a linear function of dose, is independent of the extent of DNA hydration in the range of 2.5-15 mol of water per mol of nucleotide, and is a function of the extent of hydration for DNA with more than 15 water molecules per mole of nucleotides.
the G value of the DNA hydration water is the same as that of the form of DNA in which it is bound, and the yield of free DNA bases is a linear function of dose up to 100 kGy.
the G value per water molecule is constant for the first 15 water molecules of DNA and decreases thereafter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the yield of the release of unalibrated bases is not only a function of the dose and oxygen but also a function of the extent of hydration.
the hydration of DNA plays an important role in the efficiency of DNA damage by ionizing radiation.
the hydration water of the DNA is a significant contributor to the yield of free DNA bases, and this contribution is not constant with the extent of hydration.
